$comment: Scenario 7 - cross-client convergence. THE fixture: one fresh document, three
different clients (@opto-sync/client, opto_sync_client, opto-sync-client), each
queueing a DIFFERENT payload, flushed in a deterministic order by run_all.sh:
ts  ->  dart  ->  rust
`expectedFinal` is derived by hand from the syncer.c v0.2.0 merge policy shared
by the server and all three clients. Every language asserts against it, which is
the whole point: uniform behavior is provable rather than assumed.
Derivation, key by key:
root        each payload carries a deterministic root updatedAt
(ts 2000 -> dart 3000 -> rust 4000), so queueMutation preserves
it instead of generating a process-dependent HLC. Root writes
therefore apply in the declared order and finish at 4000.
title       part of those accepted root writes -> rust's title wins.
<lang>Marker  each client contributes its own key; none collide -> all three survive.
createdAt   base 1000. No client payload sends createdAt at the root, so
nothing overwrites it. (createdAt is NOT a guarded key: fwwKeys
is unset on every tier, because FWW is a node-level veto.)
revision    guarded object. base 1000 -> ts 2000 applied -> dart 4000 applied
-> rust 3000 is STALE against 4000 and is rejected WHOLESALE, so
rust's owner/priority never land. Final: dart's, updatedAt 4000.
This is the load-bearing assertion: flush order does NOT decide a
guarded object, the timestamp does.
items       MERGE_BY_KEY on id.
'keep'     nobody touches it -> preserved verbatim.
'shared'   base 5000; ts sends 3000 (stale, rejected); dart sends
6000 (applied, deep-merged onto base so createdAt 1000
survives); rust sends 5500 (now stale vs 6000, rejected).
'ts-new' / 'dart-new' / 'rust-new' are new identities, appended in
flush order at the END of the base array.
No payload carries a top-level "id" - the document id lives in the URL.
$verifyNote: Each language's convergence phase ends by reconciling `expectedFinal` (pulled
live from the server) into its OWN payload as the local copy, and asserting the
result equals `expectedFinal`. That comparison is keyed-array-order-insensitive:
a client whose local array started as [shared, ts-new] ends up with the
server's other identities appended after its own, so the ORDER legitimately
differs while the identity set and every element's content must match exactly.
MERGE_BY_KEY is identity-based, not positional, so this is the correct notion of
equality here - the strict order-sensitive check is applied to the SERVER
document, where order is fully determined.
